feed.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node

entry.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
entry.summary:
The key management approach described aligns with grouping strategies where each set of K − 1 signers corresponds to a unique key, and that key is distributed among all participants except those within the set. A notable distinction in this implementation, specifically under `option_independent_secrets` as referenced in [lightning-blake2b/bolts17](https://github.com/lightning-blake2b/bolts17), lies in how secrets are generated and handled.
Secrets in this scheme do not originate from a single shachain seed. Instead, each secret is formed by summing outputs of pseudorandom functions (PRFs) derived from the relevant keys. This design allows each signer to independently compute their portion of the secret only when required, eliminating the need for a centralized keyblob or multiparty computation (MPC) processes for secret generation and distribution.
This decentralized approach enhances compatibility with nodelet architectures, as it removes the necessity for a central root revocation key, thereby reducing trust requirements on any particular machine. The signer rules have been scrutinized and verified for correctness, with an open invitation for peer review to identify any potential vulnerabilities.
